vendors.name: AI21 Labs
vendors.description: Jamba hybrid Mamba+Transformer family; long-context efficiency thesis.
vendors.strategy: Sell architectural efficiency (long-context cost) into enterprise + regulated buyers.
vendors.agenticCapability: Jamba Large/Mini optimised for long-context; agentic story is implementation-led.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: Solid technical specialist for long-context workloads.

vendors.name: AMD
vendors.description: The principal credible GPU alternative to NVIDIA via the Instinct MI line, increasingly adopted by hyperscalers and labs seeking supply diversification.
vendors.strategy: Win on price/performance and supply diversification; close the software gap (ROCm) versus CUDA.
vendors.agenticCapability: Not an agent vendor; an accelerator-supply alternative.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: The main lever buyers and clouds have to reduce single-source silicon risk; software maturity is the watch item.

vendors.name: AWS
vendors.description: Infrastructure-heavy AI platform provider with breadth across model choice, deployment, and cloud operations.
vendors.strategy: Win through Bedrock-style model optionality, cloud-native deployment, and enterprise infrastructure trust.
vendors.agenticCapability: Strong agent platform foundations for AWS estates; business-user assistant layer is less concentrated.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: Best considered a control plane and deployment platform, not a single assistant market-share proxy.

vendors.name: Alibaba
vendors.description: Qwen series + Alibaba Cloud Model Studio — broad multilingual + reasoning coverage.
vendors.strategy: Distribute Qwen via Alibaba Cloud and open-weight release; lead non-English benchmarks.
vendors.agenticCapability: Qwen3.5 family covers Plus / Flash variants + QwQ reasoning; agentic stack via Model Studio.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: Top-3 global frontier vendor; enterprise procurement gated by jurisdiction.

vendors.name: Andreessen Horowitz
vendors.description: Marquee venture investor (~$90B AUM) positioned across the AI stack — infrastructure (Databricks), models (OpenAI, Mistral, xAI) and applications; 2026 fundraise allocated $3.4B to AI specifically.
vendors.strategy: Invest across every layer of the AI stack as a category-conviction strategy.
vendors.agenticCapability: Not an operator; a signal of where smart capital concentrates.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: A useful signal of which categories smart capital is concentrating in, not a procurement input.

vendors.name: Anthropic
vendors.description: Frontier-reasoning + coding leader with computer-use GA and broad hyperscaler distribution. Claude Sonnet is the default model for Cursor, Aider, and GitHub Copilot Workspace; Claude Opus leads enterprise reasoning benchmarks.
vendors.strategy: Lead on reasoning + coding quality, ship computer-use and tool-use primitives, and distribute through Bedrock, Vertex, Snowflake, and Databricks rather than a packaged assistant UI.
enterpriseControls: AWS Bedrock + GCP Vertex tenant isolation
vendors.agenticCapability: Computer-use GA and tool-use leadership put Anthropic on the same agent tier as OpenAI / MSFT / AWS; buyer diligence should still inspect deployment, retention, and audit-log evidence.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: Reasoning + coding leader with a credible safety narrative; the gap on a packaged enterprise assistant is a distribution choice, not a capability one.

vendors.name: Broadcom
vendors.description: Custom-silicon (ASIC) and networking powerhouse; co-designs hyperscaler accelerators (e.g. Google TPU lineage) and supplies the switching fabric for AI data centres.
vendors.strategy: Win the custom-accelerator and networking layer that hyperscalers use to reduce NVIDIA dependence.
vendors.agenticCapability: Not an agent vendor; deep infrastructure enabler.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: A quieter but structural beneficiary of AI build-out; relevant to anyone modelling the non-NVIDIA silicon path.

vendors.name: Cerebras
vendors.description: Wafer-scale (WSE-3) inference challenger; IPO'd May 2026 (~$56B day-one valuation) anchored by a $20B+ OpenAI compute commitment with warrants up to ~10%.
vendors.strategy: Differentiate on inference latency/throughput via wafer-scale silicon; diversify away from historical single-customer concentration.
vendors.agenticCapability: Not an agent vendor; a latency/throughput and supply-diversification signal.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: An independent inference-speed alternative; the OpenAI commitment reduces but does not remove its historical concentration risk.

vendors.name: Cohere (incl. Aleph Alpha)
vendors.description: Enterprise-oriented model provider focused on secure deployment and retrieval; merged with Germany's Aleph Alpha in April 2026 to form a transatlantic sovereign-AI champion (~$20B combined, Cohere shareholders ~90%).
vendors.strategy: Focus on enterprise models, private/sovereign deployment, and knowledge-intensive workloads; combine Cohere's Command/Embed/Rerank with Aleph Alpha's Pharia/Luminous lines and STACKIT sovereign-cloud reach.
vendors.agenticCapability: Agentic layer is less visible than model and retrieval strengths; merger integration is still consolidating.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: A credible specialist when private deployment, data residency, and RAG quality matter more than suite breadth; the Aleph Alpha merger strengthens its European sovereign position.

vendors.name: CoreWeave
vendors.description: The defining 'neocloud' — a GPU-specialist cloud with a multi-billion revenue backlog (~$66B reported) and a ~$21B long-term capacity agreement with Meta through 2032.
vendors.strategy: Provide dedicated, NVIDIA-rich GPU capacity to labs and enterprises faster than hyperscalers, on long contracts.
vendors.agenticCapability: Not an agent vendor; specialist compute supply.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: A fast, NVIDIA-heavy capacity option; the balance-sheet structure (GPU-backed loans) makes it a counterparty-risk question distinct from renting from a hyperscaler.

vendors.name: Databricks
vendors.description: Data and AI platform with strong lakehouse footprint and model-building orientation.
vendors.strategy: Use data estate, open model tooling, and governance to become enterprise AI build platform.
vendors.agenticCapability: Agentic capability is strongest for data/analytics and custom enterprise build patterns.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: Strong for build-oriented enterprises that treat data governance as the AI foundation.

vendors.name: DeepSeek
vendors.description: Cost-efficient frontier reasoning lab — V4 series materially undercuts US pricing.
vendors.strategy: Win on price-per-token + reasoning quality through aggressive open release cadence.
vendors.agenticCapability: Strong reasoning benchmarks; geopolitical and data-residency caveats apply for many buyers.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: Compelling on cost-per-quality; access compliance is the deciding factor for regulated buyers.

vendors.name: Fireworks AI
vendors.description: Leading software-layer (GPU-based) inference platform optimised for throughput; reportedly in talks at ~$15B valuation, customers include Cursor, Perplexity and Notion.
vendors.strategy: Differentiate on inference throughput optimisation (FireAttention) rather than custom silicon.
vendors.agenticCapability: Hosts open models for agentic use; not an agent vendor itself.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

riskProfile: Software-optimisation moat pressured by custom silicon and hyperscaler catalogs
vendors.analystInterpretation: A throughput-optimised open-model inference option; differentiates on software, not silicon.

vendors.name: G42 / Falcon (TII)
vendors.description: Abu Dhabi's sovereign-AI holding company (~$2.3B raised; Microsoft holds a $1.5B equity stake with a board seat); the TII Falcon models are the most-cited regional open-weights frontier line, with a Cerebras-based supercomputer footprint.
vendors.strategy: Be the AI capital of the Arab world with explicit US-technology alignment; pair sovereign compute with the Falcon open-weights franchise.
vendors.agenticCapability: Agentic capability is application-embedded; the draw is sovereign compute + Arabic-native models.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: A sovereignty, compute and jurisdiction signal for Gulf and aligned-market deployments; Microsoft alignment shapes who can procure and where.

vendors.name: Glean
vendors.description: Enterprise knowledge assistant specialist with strong workplace search heritage.
vendors.strategy: Own enterprise knowledge retrieval and expand from answer engine into assistant and agent workflows.
vendors.agenticCapability: Promising knowledge-agent path; source permissioning remains a central buyer checkpoint.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: Strong category specialist for knowledge-heavy enterprises.

vendors.name: Google
vendors.description: Technically deep platform with improving enterprise packaging through Google Cloud and Workspace.
vendors.strategy: Differentiate on model research, multimodal capability, data/cloud integration, and Workspace adoption.
vendors.agenticCapability: Strong model and multimodal progress; enterprise agent operating model varies by buyer stack.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: Strong challenger where data, search, and cloud-native workloads matter.

vendors.name: Groq
vendors.description: Inference neocloud built on its LPU technology; pivoted to cloud hosting after NVIDIA's ~$20B Dec-2025 licensing/acquihire transferred its core engineering team, and is raising ~$650M.
vendors.strategy: Host inference-heavy applications on GroqCloud after the LPU IP licensing to NVIDIA.
vendors.agenticCapability: Hosts models for low-latency inference; not an agent vendor.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: Watch-list infrastructure rather than a stable dependency; the NVIDIA acquihire leaves its roadmap unproven.

vendors.name: HUMAIN
vendors.description: Saudi Arabia's national AI champion, announced May 2025 as a wholly-owned PIF subsidiary, building sovereign compute and model capability.
vendors.strategy: Build kingdom-scale sovereign compute and model capability backed by PIF capital.
vendors.agenticCapability: Very early; enterprise-readiness evidence outside the region is limited.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: A well-capitalised sovereignty and regional-access signal for Gulf-market and aligned deployments; early on enterprise readiness.

vendors.name: Harvey
vendors.description: Legal AI specialist with strong mindshare in law firms and legal departments.
vendors.strategy: Own legal knowledge work and expand into adjacent professional-services workflows.
vendors.agenticCapability: Agentic capability is valuable but should be bounded by human review and privilege controls.

industryStrength.note: Strong legal workflow fit with human review.

vendors.analystInterpretation: High-signal vertical leader; market share should be assessed in legal, not generic AI.

vendors.name: Hebbia
vendors.description: Research and document intelligence specialist with strength in high-value knowledge work.
vendors.strategy: Target analysts and deal teams with structured document intelligence and workflow depth.
vendors.agenticCapability: Agentic capability is workflow-specific and should be tested against regulated review needs.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: Compelling specialist for research-intensive teams, with confidence still shaped by reference depth.

vendors.name: IBM
vendors.description: Governance and hybrid-enterprise specialist with credibility in regulated operating environments.
vendors.strategy: Compete on trusted AI, hybrid deployment, consulting, governance, and model lifecycle management.
vendors.agenticCapability: More conservative agentic posture; strong where auditability and controls outweigh speed.
vendors.analystInterpretation: Useful benchmark for control maturity even when not the fastest growth story.

vendors.name: Lambda
vendors.description: GPU-cloud neocloud serving training and inference capacity to AI builders ($1.5B+ Series E).
vendors.strategy: Offer NVIDIA capacity (on-demand + reserved) outside the big-three hyperscalers.
vendors.agenticCapability: Not an agent vendor; compute-supply and pricing-leverage option.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: A capacity and pricing-leverage option for buyers wanting NVIDIA GPUs without hyperscaler lock-in.

vendors.name: MGX
vendors.description: UAE state-backed AI investment vehicle racing toward $100B+ AUM; co-led Anthropic's round (valuing it ~$965B) and holds a multi-billion OpenAI position.
vendors.strategy: Deploy sovereign capital at mega-round scale across frontier labs and AI infrastructure.
vendors.agenticCapability: Not an operator; Gulf sovereign-capital signal with jurisdiction implications.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: Signals Gulf sovereign capital shaping model access and data-centre build-out; relevant to sovereignty and jurisdiction questions.

vendors.name: Meta
vendors.description: Llama owner with deep open-weights distribution and Meta-AI consumer product surface.
vendors.strategy: Lead open-weights ecosystem while running Meta AI as a consumer assistant; deepen developer reach via Llama API.
vendors.agenticCapability: Llama 4 brings stronger multimodal and tool-use; enterprise productisation lags hyperscalers.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: Decisive for open-weights strategies; less of a packaged enterprise platform play.

vendors.name: Microsoft
vendors.description: Distribution leader through Microsoft 365, Azure, GitHub, and enterprise procurement reach.
vendors.strategy: Bundle AI into productivity, developer, security, and cloud workflows while shifting buyers into Azure-managed control planes.
vendors.agenticCapability: Strong copilot estate with widening agent orchestration across productivity and developer workflows.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: Likely to own the enterprise access layer, but category share must be measured by workload, not by suite reach.

vendors.name: MiniMax
vendors.description: MiniMax M2 series + her-variant for speech; consumer + B2B AI surface.
vendors.strategy: Differentiate on speech-multimodal and consumer-AI integration patterns.
vendors.agenticCapability: M2 family covers speech and multimodal; enterprise control story underdeveloped.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: Interesting multimodal contender; not yet a packaged enterprise platform.

vendors.name: Mistral
vendors.description: European model provider with strong open-weight and sovereignty positioning.
vendors.strategy: Win buyers needing model optionality, European positioning, and flexible deployment.
vendors.agenticCapability: Agentic capability depends heavily on partners and implementation layer.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: Momentum is real, but enterprise readiness should be validated workload by workload.

vendors.name: Moonshot AI
vendors.description: Kimi K2 series — known for long-context handling and reasoning depth.
vendors.strategy: Build a reasoning-and-long-context niche through K2 Thinking and platform.moonshot.ai.
vendors.agenticCapability: K2 Thinking adds reasoning; commercial enterprise track record is short.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: Strong technical contender; enterprise validation still early.

vendors.name: Moveworks
vendors.description: Employee support automation specialist focused on IT, HR, and internal service workflows.
vendors.strategy: Expand from support automation into broader enterprise service agents.
vendors.agenticCapability: Strong supervised service automation; broad autonomy depends on workflow integration depth.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: Clear value in service automation, especially where ticket deflection is measurable.

vendors.name: NVIDIA
vendors.description: The dominant AI accelerator company; GPUs (Hopper/Blackwell) and CUDA are the de-facto training and inference substrate, with DGX Cloud as a direct compute offering and a widening strategic-investment portfolio.
vendors.strategy: Hold the silicon + software (CUDA) standard, extend into systems (DGX) and networking, and use strategic investments to seed demand across labs and neoclouds.
vendors.agenticCapability: Not an agent vendor; the enabling layer beneath nearly every agentic system.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: The single highest-concentration dependency in enterprise AI. Treat NVIDIA exposure as a systemic supply risk to plan around, not a vendor to simply select.

vendors.name: Nscale
vendors.description: UK/Europe sovereign GPU-cloud neocloud (raised $1.1B+ Series B, further $2B in 2026) targeting data-residency-sensitive workloads.
vendors.strategy: Provide non-US, data-resident GPU capacity for European sovereign and regulated buyers.
vendors.agenticCapability: Not an agent vendor; sovereignty-oriented compute supply.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: A sovereignty and bargaining-leverage compute option where non-US, data-resident capacity is a procurement requirement.

vendors.name: OpenAI
vendors.description: Category shaper with strong model cadence and fast enterprise API expansion.
vendors.strategy: Lead with model quality, agent runtime, enterprise controls, and ecosystem distribution through strategic partners.
vendors.agenticCapability: Advanced supervised and autonomous agent patterns; enterprise production controls still need careful validation.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: Winning, but buyers should separate model capability from enterprise operating control.

vendors.name: Oracle
vendors.description: Enterprise application and database incumbent with AI embedded into cloud and business suites.
vendors.strategy: Use cloud infrastructure, database estate, and apps to pull AI into existing Oracle accounts.
vendors.agenticCapability: Agentic capability is more application-embedded than broad open agent platform.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: Relevant for Oracle-heavy estates; market leadership varies sharply by category.

vendors.name: Perplexity
vendors.description: AI search and answer engine with the Sonar model line; expanding from consumer search into enterprise research and knowledge workflows.
vendors.strategy: Win AI-native search and research as an application, blending first-party Sonar models with frontier model routing.
vendors.agenticCapability: Agentic research flows are emerging; enterprise controls and source-quality evidence need validation before knowledge-work scale-up.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: Best read as an AI search and research application with model-provider characteristics through Sonar, not a horizontal enterprise platform.

vendors.name: Rogo
vendors.description: Financial-services AI specialist targeting banking, investing, and research workflows.
vendors.strategy: Win regulated financial teams through domain fit, workflow language, and curated data experiences.
vendors.agenticCapability: Agentic capability should remain supervised in high-stakes finance contexts.
vendors.analystInterpretation: Interesting vertical specialist; evaluate evidence depth before enterprise-scale rollout.

vendors.name: SAP
vendors.description: ERP and business-process incumbent embedding AI into finance, supply chain, HR, and procurement.
vendors.strategy: Defend and extend system-of-record workflows through embedded assistants and process intelligence.
vendors.agenticCapability: Agentic capability is strongest in governed business processes rather than open-ended autonomy.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: Strong for SAP-centric operating models; do not confuse ERP reach with frontier AI share.

vendors.name: Sakana AI
vendors.description: Tokyo-based lab building Japan's domestic frontier-model capability with a distinctive evolutionary/merged-model research approach.
vendors.strategy: Anchor Japan's domestic frontier capability with a research-led, efficiency-oriented model approach.
vendors.agenticCapability: Research-stage; enterprise productisation and controls evidence are early.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: A regional-sovereignty and research-diversity signal more than a current enterprise default.

vendors.name: Salesforce
vendors.description: CRM workflow owner with strong access to sales, service, and customer data.
vendors.strategy: Embed AI agents into CRM workflows and monetise via packaged customer-facing productivity outcomes.
vendors.agenticCapability: Strong domain-agent narrative in sales and service; cross-enterprise autonomy requires validation.

industryStrength.note: Strong CRM data and workflow position.

vendors.analystInterpretation: A sector leader for customer workflows, but not a universal enterprise AI platform.

vendors.name: Sequoia Capital
vendors.description: Long-standing frontier-AI venture backer (~$56B AUM); raised a ~$7B expansion fund in 2026 for late-stage AI bets including OpenAI and Anthropic.
vendors.strategy: Back frontier labs and AI infrastructure as a late-stage category-conviction play.
vendors.agenticCapability: Not an operator; a category-conviction signal.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: Read Sequoia's concentration as category conviction; it does not bear on enterprise deployment fitness.

vendors.name: ServiceNow
vendors.description: Workflow automation incumbent with strong IT, HR, and enterprise service management footprint.
vendors.strategy: Position AI agents as workflow execution inside systems of record for service operations.
vendors.agenticCapability: Good supervised workflow-agent fit; autonomy should be staged around approval and audit paths.

industryStrength.note: Strong ITSM and service workflow ownership.

vendors.analystInterpretation: A practical enterprise agent player where workflows already live in ServiceNow.

vendors.name: Snowflake
vendors.description: Data cloud incumbent embedding AI into analytics, apps, and governed enterprise data workflows.
vendors.strategy: Turn governed data estate into AI applications, search, and application-development layer.
vendors.agenticCapability: Agentic capability is emerging around governed data and app workflows.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: Strong data-layer contender; category share differs greatly between data AI and assistant markets.

vendors.name: SoftBank
vendors.description: One of the largest single-cheque AI investors; committed ~$30B to OpenAI's 2026 round (with further $10B tranches) and co-anchors the Stargate data-centre JV.
vendors.strategy: Concentrate mega-scale capital where compute and model access follow; pair investment with infrastructure JVs.
vendors.agenticCapability: Not an operator; a capital-and-distribution signal.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: Where SoftBank concentrates capital, compute and model access tend to follow; a capital-flow signal, not a procurement input.

vendors.name: TSMC
vendors.description: The foundry that manufactures the leading-edge chips for NVIDIA, AMD, Apple and the hyperscalers; the physical bottleneck of the entire AI hardware supply chain.
vendors.strategy: Hold the leading-edge process lead and capacity that every fabless AI-chip designer depends on.
vendors.agenticCapability: Not an agent vendor; the foundation beneath the silicon layer.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: The deepest single point in the AI supply chain; geopolitical and capacity risk here propagates to every chip vendor above it.

vendors.name: Together AI
vendors.description: Open-model inference and fine-tuning cloud; a flagship host for Llama, DeepSeek, Qwen and Mistral ($305M Series B).
vendors.strategy: Be the open-weight deployment route when self-hosting is impractical but closed APIs are undesirable.
vendors.agenticCapability: Hosts open models for agentic use; not an agent vendor itself.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: The open-weight deployment path for enterprises avoiding both self-hosting and closed APIs.

vendors.name: Writer
vendors.description: Enterprise generative AI platform focused on brand-safe content, workflows, and knowledge apps.
vendors.strategy: Differentiate through enterprise content workflows, governance, and business-user tooling.
vendors.agenticCapability: Agentic workflows are emerging around content and knowledge operations.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: Potential winner in governed content workflows, less proven as a universal platform.

vendors.name: Z.ai
vendors.description: Zhipu / Z.ai — GLM-5.1 frontier model; significant in Chinese enterprise + research market.
vendors.strategy: Anchor GLM as Chinese frontier alternative with English/multilingual coverage expanding.
vendors.agenticCapability: GLM-5.1 multimodal capable; broader agent stack underdeveloped vs frontier US labs.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: Relevant for jurisdictional diversity; Western enterprise readiness limited.

vendors.name: xAI
vendors.description: Frontier lab with Grok model line and Memphis Colossus compute build-out; investor + governance opacity remain a constraint.
vendors.strategy: Win on compute scale, real-time signal (X integration), and aggressive model cadence.
vendors.agenticCapability: Grok and tool-use shipping; enterprise track record and audit story thin.

industryStrength.note: Needs privacy and clinical workflow evidence.

vendors.analystInterpretation: High-beta frontier contender; enterprise readiness lags the leading set.
